description: D9: every open register low scheduled for 3.8.0 and every carried P143 review finding (BUG-31-z9j), grouped one task per file cluster with one shared fix per recurring class. Plan: quality-gates-internal/plans/2026-11-02-low-batch-3-8-0.md.
desiredOutcome: Every open low scheduled for 3.8.0 is fixed or closed with a reason, and BUG-31-z9j is closed

findings.issue: No case covers the new refusal of an --answer sent to a set-aside sign-off decision. rf1/rf2 cover only the no-answer path: dispatch, and the blocked twin. If lines 9408-9411 are deleted, most answers are still refused, but by answer_refusal's different 'no decision is pending' text. `--answer sign-off --reason` would instead take _pending_route's advance route (pending is None) and drive on. The PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE sentence claiming the refusal cites rf1/rf2, and neither case reaches it.
findings.resolution: Add a case (rf12): with the drive at the triage, add a task with the verb, then run `next --answer sign-off --reason S`. Assert exit 2, the added task's id in the text, no pending left in state, and the phase not signed off. Cite it beside the guide sentence.

findings.issue: decline_answer's docstring says 'The drive goes on to any task still open - the remedy a human added', and db2 pins that by calling decline_answer directly. Through `next`, a human who adds the remedy task first and then answers `--answer decline --reason <words>` is now refused at drive_locked:9408, because the decision is set aside while the remedy is ready. Their words never reach state['declined'], so the summary loses the no. That branch of decline_answer is now reachable only for an open task that cannot run. DECLINE_REMEDY's order (decline first, then add) still works.
findings.resolution: Either let `decline` through on a set-aside decision (record the words in `declined`, pop phaseGate, then drive the runnable task), or reword the docstring and db2 so they describe an open task that cannot run. Add a drive-level case for whichever is chosen.

findings.issue: _status_facts.unmet_refs already folds a blocked phase's refs into each task's entry as '<ref> (phase)' (_status_facts.py:1424). not_ready_why then appends unmet[phase_id] a second time. A wave member dropped because its phase gained a blocker therefore prints that ref twice in the dropped-from-wave line: 'waits on P9 (phase), P9'.
findings.resolution: Read unmet.get(task_id) alone, since it already carries the phase's refs, and fall back to 'nothing the plan names' only when it is empty.

findings.issue: The task widens the ruff path list in tools/verify.sh to include .claude/hooks, but CLAUDE.md:210 (the 'Tests' command block, 'the commands a change most often reruns by hand') and the plan's meta.buildCommands.lint still spell `ruff check plugins/audit tools tests`. A contributor or a build-command-driven gate following either runs a narrower ruff than verify.sh and would not see an unused import under .claude/hooks - the very class this task closes. The executor reported this as left for the orchestrator; it is a changed shape crossing into untouched files.
findings.resolution: Add `.claude/hooks` to the ruff line at CLAUDE.md:210 and set meta.buildCommands.lint through `/audit:task build-command` (or drop the hand copy and point at `verify.sh --list`).

add: tests/test__tree_stamp.py: _write_shapes returns (name, exc) and the SKIPPED line prints the errno; the skip's absent argument is a fact that can be false

outcome.technical: tests/test__tree_stamp.py only. _write_shapes now returns (name, exc) pairs. New TAB_REFUSAL_ERRNOS = (errno.EINVAL,) (what open() raises on Windows for a name NTFS forbids), _refusal_text(exc) -> '[Errno N] <strerror>', _skip_tab_case(check, label, refusal) calls _harness.skip with the mechanism 'this filesystem refused to create a file named %r: [Errno N] <strerror>' and absent = exc.errno in TAB_REFUSAL_ERRNOS (false, so the skip FAILS, for any other errno or none). _refusing() takes an optional exc; _recording() is a check that keeps calls. TAB_LABEL holds the tso3 label once. Cases: tso4 rewritten to require [(TAB_NAME, the very OSError raised)]; tso6 new (EINVAL refusal -> one recorded line, passing, starting '<tso3 label> SKIPPED HERE' and ending ': [Errno 22] Invalid argument'); tso7 new (EACCES and an errno-less OSError -> skip recorded as failing, line carries '[Errno 13] Permission denied'). Gate: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__tree_stamp.py tools/_suite.py exit 0, run twice ('2/2 files ok, 102 cases'; suite 67 cases). ruff check tests/test__tree_stamp.py exit 0; vermin -t=3.8- exit 0; prose_number_claims/house_style_violations report nothing for the file. Simulated Windows (the suite's _write patched to raise OSError(EINVAL, 'Invalid argument') for the tab name, _one_listing_cases run through _harness.run): exit 0, 7/7, and printed: PASS tso3 a name holding a tab is read whole in both halves SKIPPED HERE - this filesystem refused to create a file named 'tab\there.txt': [Errno 22] Invalid argument. WINDOWS, for the owner (not run here, unverified on a real NTFS): from the checkout root, py -3 tests\test__tree_stamp.py --selftest ; expected exit 0 and the line above verbatim among the PASS lines (find it with: py -3 tests\test__tree_stamp.py --selftest | findstr /C:"tso3"). If Windows raises a different errno for the name, tso3 prints FAIL with that errno in the line, which is the new behaviour working, and TAB_REFUSAL_ERRNOS is the one place to widen. Plan gate: writing the probe at <tree>/probe/mutations.py was refused ('[require-plan] probe/mutations.py is outside task P155.4, the task this worktree is bound to ... Only that task's files are open here.'), so the probe lives at <scratchpad>/probe/mutations.py (takes --root, asserts one anchor occurrence and the landing, purges __pycache__, output to files, baseline green first, sha256 restore). Run it against a COPY (rsync of tests/ plugins/ tools/), not a shared tree. Dependants: .github/sweep-costs.json (path) still correct - the added cases are pure, no new git fixture, suite still ~2.7s against its 16.1 figure; plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_tree_stamp.py (path) still correct - untouched, its docstring only points at this suite; tests/test_stamp_verification.py (basename) still correct - it shares only same-named private helpers (_cases, _git, _seeded_repo, _recorder_dirty_cases), imports nothing from this suite, and none of those changed; tools/_suite.py ran green in the gate (35 cases). Class sweep, left: an AST walk over tests/*.py for _harness.skip(...) with a literal True as absent prints 50 sites (command: the ast walk in this session, rerunnable); most sit under a branch whose condition is the evidence, but test__output.py:1096 (rt3) and test_stamp_verification.py:5868 (sw11) grade any caught exception as absence, the same shape this task fixed - outside this task's files, not edited; worth a Faults row.
outcome.descriptive: The tree-stamp suite's tab-name skip now prints the errno that caused it and fails instead of skipping when the refusal is not the filesystem's name rule.

verifiedBy: tso4 (rewritten): a refusing builder returns the refused name paired with the very OSError it raised, every other shape built
tso6: the tab-name skip line ends with ': [Errno 22] Invalid argument' and passes for an EINVAL refusal
tso7: an EACCES refusal and an errno-less OSError make the tab-name skip fail, the line carrying '[Errno 13] Permission denied'

redFirst.basis: None owed: the task is mode regression with tests.expectRedFirst false. The submit helper also cannot separate the two versions here, because the fix lives entirely in the declared test file (tests/test__tree_stamp.py), so HEAD with that file copied over it is byte-identical to the fixed tree. The red was watched by mutation instead, in a scratch copy of the tree (never the shared tree): python3 <scratchpad>/probe/mutations.py --root <copy> exit 0, baseline tso4/tso6/tso7 PASS, then m1 builder keeps the name only (the unfixed shape) -> FAIL tso4; m2 skip line without the error -> FAIL tso6; m3 absent=bool(refusal) (the unfixed always-true evidence) -> FAIL tso7; m4 over-fire absent never true -> FAIL tso6; file restored and sha256-checked after every row. Run three times (09:1x UTC), 4 of 4 rows red each time.
redFirst.at: 2026-11-02T09:17:38Z (second probe run); third run after the TAB_LABEL refactor, also 4 of 4
